risk_flags.note: Corpus provides only compressed macro framing, limiting confidence in detailed actor calibration.
Scenario concerns a real institution, but content is analytical forecasting rather than targeting or persuasion.
Resolution depends narrowly on the target range level; implementation changes or rhetoric alone must not be mistaken for yes.
Outcome is materially contingent on late incoming inflation and labor data not included in the corpus.

simulation_brief.summary: Late-2025 FOMC decision environment with mixed labor-market softening and inflation-above-target pressures. Markets discuss a possible quarter-point cut, while policymakers emphasize data dependence. Terminal question is whether the federal funds target range is lower immediately after the December 10, 2025 meeting statement than immediately before.
uncertainty_notes: Source packet is sparse and high-level.
No detailed inflation, employment, or financial-conditions data are provided.
No explicit vote commitments or internal dissents are described at T0.

sociology_baseline.note: Actors update within established reaction-function frames rather than on extreme narratives.
Large repricing likely requires clear late-data surprise or strong communication shift.
Most of the public is low attention and not actively expressing views on the meeting outcome.
Experts cluster into easing-watch and inflation-caution interpretive camps.
Meeting-outcome narratives strengthen when reinforced by both data and official messaging.
Hawk-dove identities matter but are moderated by institutional discipline and consensus norms.
Attention remains episodic until major data releases or the meeting itself.

sociology_prompt_influences.description: Official communication stresses contingency on incoming data rather than commitment.
Labor softening and above-target inflation pull expectations in opposite directions.
Only a lower target range after the statement counts as a yes; implementation-detail changes do not.
A quarter-point cut is actively discussed but not settled.
